story: On Magnolia Loop on a breezy, clear Thursday just after noon, Gary is determined to finally file his Architectural Review paperwork, but first he wants to sort out Donna's pickleball dinks. Donna is eager to get on court before the lunch crowd arrives and offers to carry Gary's water bottle to help him move along. Hal, content in the warm 76-degree air, promises Rosa he'll bring a pan of cornbread and his sturdy chair to her Saturday supper, while Rosa, determined to plan the evening, presses him for a yes.

gary.thought_process: Donna's ready to head to the rec center for dink practice, Hal's asking about the Architectural Review paperwork, and Rosa has Saturday handled. I already confirmed dinner at six with Rosa, so no need to repeat that. Hal's nudge is fair: L-01 says my cart mods need approval before I flip any switches. I checked the bulletin board last tick, and the real filing is probably at Town Hall. Best move is to answer both of them in one go: tell Hal I'm filing today, then walk with Donna to the rec center. I want the parade lights legal and approved, and I don't want to let Donna down.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal. You're right, I'm filing the Architectural Review paperwork today, no more stalling. Let me get Donna's dinks sorted first and then I'll walk it in.

donna.thought_process: I told Gary at tick 151 to grab his paddle and head to the rec center, but he's still at the bulletin board dealing with Hal's cart paperwork. Hal is pressing him and Rosa is gathering her Saturday crowd, so I shouldn't repeat my invitation. A little nudge to get him moving fits, plus I can keep it light for Hal's sake. The courts are limited to two hours per party, so I want to claim our slot before the lunch crowd does. I'll give Gary a short, friendly push to wrap up and walk over with me.

parameters.content: Finish up with Hal, Gary, then let's move. I want us on court before the lunch crowd grabs it, and I'll carry your water bottle if that's what it takes.

hal.thought_process: Rosa asked what I can't eat or what dish to bring, and she's standing right here waiting on an answer. I haven't responded yet, so that comes first. I'm soft on her dinner even if I'll never say so. A solid, practical contribution suits a supply sergeant: bread or a sturdy pan of cornbread, plus the chair I already promised to haul over. No restrictions to speak of. The L-01 report is filed, so I don't need to nag Gary again this tick.

parameters.content: Nothing I can't eat, Rosa, I'm not fussy. I'll bring a pan of cornbread and that sturdy chair of mine, since your porch is short a good seat.

rosa.thought_process: Gary, Donna, and Hal are all right here on the street. Gary already swore to Donna he's coming Saturday at six, and I asked Hal last tick and he hasn't given me his answer on food or a dish. Donna's lemon bars are covered. Gary and Donna are heading to the courts, so I should pin down Hal's answer now, briefly, without re-asking Gary. Hal's a blunt man who cares about the cart paperwork, so I'll keep it short and practical, and give him something to say yes or no to.

parameters.content: Hal, I still need your answer for Saturday at six. Gary and Donna are both in, so tell me yes, tell me what you can't eat, and I'll plan around it.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
